..
Issued at 415 AM CDT Mon Oct 5 2026

Exiting ridge of high pressure will be replaced by a weak 
trough and surface low today. A warm front will lift through to 
begin the day and bring warm temperatures and breezy southerly 
winds. Some hi-res models try to develop a few showers this 
morning as this warm front lifts through. Weak instability could
even hint at a few isolated thunderstorms possible. However, a 
surge of dry air will make the chances for any shower or 
thunderstorm activity low today thus kept a mainly dry forecast.
This dry air is expected to lower afternoon RH values into the 
teens and 20s across the southwest. Southerly winds shifting to 
a breezy westerly wind could bring some near critical fire 
weather concerns in this area. See the Fire Weather Discussion 
for more details. High temperatures today will continue to be 
above normal and warm into the 70s for most areas with some 80s 
in the southwest. As the trough and weak cold front moves 
through a shift to westerly winds will be found from west to 
east later today through tonight. The rest of tonight then looks
mostly clear to partly cloudy with dry conditions. Mild lows in
the 40s to lower 50s look to continue for tonight. A more 
subtle yet still post frontal day is then in store for Tuesday. 
Temperatures will cool slightly yet still remain above normal 
and generally in the upper 60s to upper 70s. There could be some
breezy northwest winds at times, although winds overall do not 
look as breezy as today. With this dry pattern, low RH values in
the 20s will again be found across the southwest. This could 
provide for a brief period of near critical fire weather 
conditions across the southwest, depending how strong the winds 
become. Surface high with northwest flow aloft is then expected
for Tuesday night. Cooler lows in the upper 30s to mid 40s are 
forecast, with low temperatures somewhat dependent on how much 
cloud cover is found within the northwest flow aloft. Dry 
conditions will remain in place Tuesday night, limiting any fog 
threat.

A broad surface high then looks to remain across the state
Wednesday and Thursday, with northwest flow aloft. Overall this
will result in mainly dry conditions, with light winds, and
continued mild temperatures. Some cooler temperatures may be
found each morning depending on cloud cover, with forecast lows
in the mid 30s to mid 40s. Another broad area of low pressure
could then return later in the week into the start of the
weekend. Right now the forecast would indicate North Dakota is 
in the warm and mainly dry sector of this low. The result could
be continued above normal temperatures, mainly dry conditions,
and breezy winds at times.  

Attention then turns to later in the weekend into early next 
week. Clusters still indicating the next broad trough pattern 
moving into the region. There is medium to high confidence this 
pattern shift brings cooler temperatures which is also indicated
in the NBM temperature spreads overall going on a lowering 
trend although do have large spreads at times. This could bring
the next widespread chance for freeze conditions especially 
early next week. The larger uncertainty is precipitation 
chances. NBM keeps in low to moderate chances Sunday into early 
next week. Clusters differ with some showing a broad trough 
pattern moving through, others showing more of a cut off low 
setting up to the west, while a few split the difference and 
indicate more of a split flow pattern is possible. Thus will 
maintain the low to medium chances for precipitation until more 
confidence can be achieved. Some deterministic models showing 
snow is possible with these precipitation chances. This will be 
highly dependent on how much cold air can enter into the area, 
and confidence in any accumulations this far out is low. This 
potentially more active pattern could also bring some breezy 
winds at times, although increasing RH values should limit any 
fire weather concerns.
